proposal.description: flag_out flip compares the disagreement count against the counter's sizing limit CNT_MAX (the assert time) instead of the target for the pending direction, so the release direction is forgotten
proposal.reason: With the default parameters (ASSERT > RELEASE), a release attempt clears the counter at RELEASE_CLKS-1 and never reaches ASSERT_CLKS-1. Once flag_out is high, it never goes low again, even when flag_in stays low indefinitely.

proposal.description: The disagreement counter's clear-on-qualify limit uses CNT_MAX instead of the selected target, so the count is not restarted on the edge a release qualifies
proposal.reason: When flag_out releases and flag_in goes high again on the very next clock, the counter keeps counting up from RELEASE_CLKS. flag_out then asserts after only ASSERT_CLKS-RELEASE_CLKS clocks of high input instead of ASSERT_CLKS.

proposal.description: The restart on agreement is applied only when flag_in is high, so an aborted assert attempt (flag_in back low while flag_out is low) leaves its partial count in place
proposal.reason: While flag_out is low, short high glitches on flag_in now add up across gaps instead of each restarting from zero. flag_out asserts once the glitches total ASSERT_CLKS clocks, even though no single pulse was that long: a false fault from switching-node pickup.

proposal.description: target_clks is written as a terminal count (qualification time minus one), while both compares still subtract one again, so every transition qualifies one clock early
proposal.reason: In both directions, flag_out now follows a steady new level of flag_in after ASSERT_CLKS-1 or RELEASE_CLKS-1 clocks of disagreement instead of ASSERT_CLKS or RELEASE_CLKS. The edge reaches the supervisor one clock early.
